rounds.text: Nidhi Granites Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of just 23.2x while delivering exceptional elite-tier returns on capital, including an extraordinary ROCE of 43.94% to 51.0% and an ROE of 33.79% to 41.0%, drastically outperforming sector benchmarks [E1, E6, E10, E12, E13]. Fundamental momentum is explosive and vastly outpacing the stock price, evidenced by a 156% compounded profit growth over 5 years and a 162% profit growth in the trailing twelve months, alongside operating margins expanding by 18 percentage points over three years to 23% [E17, E19, E27, E43]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 478 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 43.1% over the market price of Rs 272, with management explicitly guiding that the company is likely to grow with accelerated momentum [E40, E41, E60]. The balance sheet remains robust and conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.10x and a comfortable current ratio of 2.40x, while working capital requirements have efficiently compressed from 72.5 days to 58.0 days [E34, E35, E47]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 7.82x to 7.83x against a sector benchmark of 1.59x, the dividend yield stands at 0.00%, and compounded share price growth over the past year is down by 34% [E2, E4, E7, E23].

Despite recent profit metrics, investors are paying a steep price-to-book multiple of 7.82x on a book value of ₹ 34.8 against a share price of ₹ 272 [E2], and the stock has suffered a compounded share price decline of -34% over the past year [E23]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and the directors did not recommend any dividend for the year under review, leaving shareholders with zero cash returns despite reported profits [E4, E70]. Underlying earnings stability is also questionable given that quarterly operating margins are flagged as inconsistent over the last two quarters [E30], and the company historically faced challenges in its core business activities that forced a shift toward trading in securities [E75]. The business is also exposed to external vulnerabilities, with management noting that prospects are closely linked to local economic conditions and escalating geopolitical hostilities [E73]. On a standalone basis, the picture weakens further as the company incurred a loss of Rs. 148.56 Lakhs after providing for depreciation during the year under review [E69]. Conceded: the company delivered strong 5-year profit growth of 156% [E17, E46] and maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10x [E34].

Conceded: the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% and no dividend was recommended for the year under review [E4, E70], and the stock price declined -34% over the past year [E23]. However, the steep price-to-book multiple of 7.82x [E2] is fully justified by extraordinary returns on capital, including an ROE of 33.79% to 41.0% and an ROCE reaching up to 43.94% and 51.0%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. While the bear highlights inconsistent quarterly operating margins over two quarters [E30], the broader trend shows yearly operating margins consistently increasing over the last 5 years with TTM operating margins expanding to 23% [E27, E29]. Conceded: the company incurred a standalone loss of Rs. 148.56 Lakhs [E69], but this is eclipsed by powerful multi-year compounding where 5-year profit growth reached 156% against a share price growth of only 50%, proving that fundamentals are massively outpacing the stock and leaving a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs. 478 with a 43.1% margin of safety [E17, E21, E40, E41, E43]. Finally, concerns regarding core business challenges and geopolitical exposure [E73, E75] are countered by a solid balance sheet carrying a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10x [E34], improved working capital requirements down to 58 days [E47], and a promising outlook with the addition of the Fintech business and expected accelerated momentum [E60, E63].

Conceded: the company boasts multi-year profit growth of 156% over five years and a TTM operating margin of 23% [E17, E27]. However, the bull's dismissal of the standalone loss of Rs. 148.56 Lakhs after depreciation [E69] ignores the underlying volatility of a business that historically admitted to facing challenges in its core activities, forcing a pivot toward trading in securities to deploy resources [E75]. While the bull celebrates an ROE of up to 41.0% [E13] and an intrinsic value model [E40], this sits alongside a -34% one-year share price decline [E23] and an inconsistent quarterly operating margin trend over the last two quarters [E30]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the rich valuation by pointing to high returns [E9, E10], but the evidence shows a steep price-to-book multiple of 7.82x [E2] and zero dividend yield [E4] while insiders provide a corporate guarantee of ₹5 Crores to a wholly owned subsidiary [E72]. Finally, the optimistic outlook regarding a new Fintech business [E63] is clouded by the reality that the company's business prospects remain closely tied to escalating geopolitical hostilities and local economic environments [E73].
